newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan cuts bread prices by 10 percent.
newsitem.headline: Jordan cuts bread prices by 10 percent.

text.p: Jordan cut bread prices by 10 percent on Wednesday, cashing in on a weak world grain market to soften price hikes that sparked riots in August.

The state news agency Petra said the price of bread, staple food for millions of poorer Jordanians, was reduced by 20 fils (three U.S. cents) to 170 fils per kilo, or 200 fils for bread made from higher quality flour.

Jordan, following advice from the International Monetary Fund, virtually doubled bread prices overnight in August to slash its ballooning bill for subsidies as world grain prices reached record highs. World prices have since fallen.
Its modest compensation offer to the most needy failed to prevent the worst outbreak of unrest in the impoverished south since riots in 1989, also sparked by price rises.
The drop in prices is in keeping with a promise to reduce local prices of basic commodities Jordan imports, including wheat and sugar, when world grain markets soften.

In November Jordan reduced by 7.5 percent the price of animal fodder sold to the country's livestock owners to soften a 33 percent price rise in yellow corn in August that accompanied the bread price hike.
Many pastoral Jordanians are nomadic Bedouins for whom livestock rearing is the main source of income.
